bottom_line: Lenient rate control vs strict rate control was noninferior for the primary composite outcome at 3 years (12.9% vs 14.9%; absolute difference, −2.0 percentage points [90% CI, −7.6 to 3.5]).
implications: With 3-year cumulative incidence 12.9% vs 14.9% (absolute difference −2.0 percentage points; 90% CI, −7.6 to 3.5; hazard ratio 0.84 [90% CI, 0.58–1.21]), the document supports that lenient rate control was noninferior to strict rate control for the composite primary outcome over up to 3 years; it does not establish superiority, and it does not provide evidence beyond the reported follow-up duration.

major_points.text: Prospective, randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial comparing lenient vs strict rate-control strategies in permanent atrial fibrillation.
major_points.quote: The Rate Control Efficacy in Permanent Atrial Fibrillation: a Comparison between Lenient versus Strict Rate Control II (RACE II) study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial

major_points.text: Rate-control targets: lenient group resting HR <110 bpm; strict group resting HR <80 bpm and exercise HR <110 bpm during moderate exercise.
major_points.quote: lenient rate-control strategy (resting heart rate <110 beats per minute) or a strict rate-control strategy (resting heart rate <80 beats per minute and heart rate during moder- ate exercise <110 beats per minute).

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite including cardiovascular death, HF hospitalization, stroke, systemic embolism, major bleeding, and life-threatening arrhythmic events.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, hospitalization for heart failure, and stroke, systemic embolism, bleeding, and life-threatening arrhythmic events.

major_points.text: Primary outcome at 3 years: 12.9% (lenient) vs 14.9% (strict), meeting prespecified noninferiority criterion.
major_points.quote: The estimated cumulative incidence of the primary outcome at 3 years was 12.9% in the lenient-control group and 14.9% in the strict-control group, with an absolute difference with respect to the lenient-control group of −2.0 percentage points (90% confidence interval, −7.6 to 3.5

major_points.text: More patients met the heart-rate target(s) with lenient control and with fewer total visits.
major_points.quote: More patients in the lenient-control group met the heart-rate target or targets (304 [97.7%], vs. 203 [67.0%] in the strict-control group; P<0.001) with fewer total visits (75 [median, 0], vs. 684 [median, 2]; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Symptoms and adverse events were similar between groups.
major_points.quote: The frequencies of symptoms and adverse events were similar in the two groups.

analysis_methods.text: Primary efficacy analysis was in the intention-to-treat population.

analysis_methods.text: Planned 80% power to rule out an absolute increase of 10 percentage points (one-sided alpha 0.05).
analysis_methods.quote: a re- quirement that the study had 80% power to rule out an absolute increase of 10 percentage points

analysis_methods.text: Initial sample size plan: 250 patients in each group with median follow-up 2.5 years (allowing <5% attrition).
analysis_methods.quote: A sample size of 250 patients in each group with a median follow-up of 2.5 years satisfied the sta- tistical requirements, allowing for an attrition rate of less than 5% of patients.

analysis_methods.text: Because the primary outcome occurred less frequently than anticipated, sample size increased to 300 in each group and follow-up extended to June 30, 2009 (max 3 years).
analysis_methods.quote: We increased the number of patients to 300 in each group and ex- tended the follow-up period to June 30, 2009, with a maximum duration of 3 years.

analysis_methods.text: Noninferiority assessed using Kaplan–Meier estimated 3-year cumulative incidences and the upper bound of the 90% CI for absolute difference (<10 percentage points).
analysis_methods.quote: To satisfy the criterion for noninferiority, the upper bound of the 90% confidence interval for the absolute difference between the two treatment groups in the estimated rate of the primary out- come needed to be less than 10 percentage points

analysis_methods.text: Hazard ratio also reported after statistical adjustment for coronary artery disease, statin use, and diastolic blood pressure.
analysis_methods.quote: The haz- ard ratio was 0.80 (90% CI, 0.55 to 1.17) after statistical adjustment for the unbalanced distri- bution of the presence of coronary artery disease, the use of statins, and the diastolic blood pres- sure.

criticisms.text: Cannot rule out differences if stricter separation of achieved heart rates, tighter control around 110 bpm in lenient group, or longer follow-up beyond 3 years.
criticisms.quote: We can- not rule out the possibility that we would have found significant differences between the two groups had we used a more effective means of strict rate control and had we kept heart rates just below 110 beats per minute in the lenient-con- trol group or if we had followed patients beyond 3 years.

criticisms.text: Excluded patients with a previous stroke, resulting in a low-risk study population, which may have contributed to lower-than-expected event rate.
criticisms.quote: Thus, we ex- cluded patients with a previous stroke, resulting in a low-risk study population. These choices may have resulted in the lower-than-expected prima- ry outcome event rate.

criticisms.text: Study may not capture differences in severity of symptoms between groups even if prevalence was similar.
criticisms.quote: Although the prevalence of symptoms was similar in the two groups in our study, we cannot rule out potential differences in the severity of symptoms between the groups.
